comments.author: @andrewrivett3366
comments.text:
I was there in 2025 before the fuel was completely cut off.  I rented a car and made a tank of gas last me the week.  I stayed in an Airbnb and that was difficult because it wasn't all inclusive and I didn't have enough cash.  The fact that hardly anybody accepted credit cards wasn't an issue that anybody wrote about.  

I tried to buy some bread and this old lady tried to sell me sex instead.  There was no bread in the grocery store  but it doesn't deserve to be called a grocery store (Mercado) because they don't even have the basics.  Just lots of certain items like beer and rum and some canned fish.  It just depends upon what the government distributes and that's seldom what you want or what you need.  

Somehow the people still seemed relatively happy but it was more like a resigned acceptance that nothing works, there's not enough of anything and it's not getting better.  It's getting worse.  So they just put up with it.  They don't have a lot of choice.  

First thing I'd try to do if I lived there would be to get to any other place except maybe Haiti because I can't imagine living under those conditions.  I've been to some poor places in the world but Cuban conditions just look worse because as a visitor I couldn't figure how things would get any better.  The country is broke.  Even tourism is finished now.  They don't have fuel.  They don't have enough food.  Their infrastructure (water, electricity) and services like health care are in crisis.  Power outages frequently and water stops running out of the taps at any time.  The resorts were insulated from these realities because they had their own generators.  So a lot of tourists didn't see what I saw.  

It just proves that people are extremely adaptable animals and that we can be conditioned for the most part to accept the unacceptable.  

They have the freedom to leave the island but not the money so most of them are stuck living in these conditions until who knows when.  

Tourists who bring consumer staples and tylenol or whatever are well meaning but this is like putting a bandage on a ruptured aorta.

I won't go back.  It's too depressing.  I feel bad for those poor people.
